analysis: What changed vs the 8:00 AM brief: the morning fade became a second leg down. SPY broke below $750 to a $745.20 session low and sits at $749.15 (-1.05%) as of 11:52 AM ET, with the Nasdaq 100 down 2% and the S&P 500 down 0.85%. Nvidia broke below $160 and kept sliding to a $158.39 low (-4.04% at $159.47), and the chip rout broadened rather than contained itself: AMD -7.2%, Broadcom down more than 6% after a Redburn downgrade, and the SOX down about 5%. Fed's Collins concluded her remarks with a benign read (markets stable and functioning well, firms seeing strong demand and expecting to hire), offering no pushback on the three-hike repricing; Bowman's 10:50 AM ET remarks produced no market-moving headlines in coverage. The 10-year held ~5.13% and the VIX held just above 20, so the selloff remains equity-led, not a fresh rate spike. Apple (+0.76%, after a new 52-week high of $360.83) and Meta (+1.08%) are still the only green megacaps. Signal vs noise: the broadening chip selloff and the VIX holding above 20 are real — the market is pricing the hiking path and the Nvidia governance overhang over the PPI print. Collins's calm tone and the Cisco guidance raise are background, not tape-movers.

headlines.headline: The selloff deepened into late morning: S&P 500 -0.85%, Nasdaq 100 -2%, Russell 2000 -0.85% as of ~11:13 AM ET. SPY is $749.15 (-1.05% vs Thursday's $757.12 close) at 11:52 AM ET after opening at $760.07 and touching a $745.20 low; the Dow is the relative holdout at -0.14% on futures.
headlines.why_it_matters: A second leg down after the opening fade, with SPY breaking below $750, means the PPI relief is fully spent — the tape is now trading the Fed hiking path, not the inflation print.

headlines.headline: Nvidia broke below $160 and kept sliding: $159.47 (-4.04%) at 11:52 AM ET after opening at $169.91 and touching a $170.00 high, with a session low of $158.39. The stock is down ~12% this week and -27.9% over the past month. Earnings are Tue Nov 17 (Kress's first call as interim CEO); consensus expects ~$111.2B revenue and ~$2.52 EPS.
headlines.why_it_matters: Three failed bounces in one session and a break of $160 show sellers are in control into earnings — the governance overhang is now compounding with margin and AI-spending doubts.

headlines.headline: The chip rout broadened: AMD fell 7.2% after a five-session rise, Broadcom fell more than 6% after a Redburn downgrade, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) is down about 5%. Cerebras is the lone offset, +18% after lifting its FY26 revenue forecast.
headlines.why_it_matters: The weakness is spreading across the whole chip complex, not just NVDA — a sector-wide AI-valuation reset, with only the Microsoft-linked Cerebras story bucking it.

headlines.headline: Microsoft's 365 outage is into day two and is still disrupting businesses and governments globally: Teams service health is restored and email delivery is improving, but the incident is not declared resolved and the focus is now clearing the email queue and backlog; no root cause yet and no cyberattack indicated. MSFT is $521.68 (-0.25%) at 11:52 AM ET.
headlines.why_it_matters: Partial recovery is keeping the stock near flat, but a second day without a root cause keeps the reliability question open for enterprise customers.

headlines.headline: Fed's Collins concluded her remarks saying she is seeing evidence financial markets are stable and functioning well, with some firms seeing strong demand and expecting to hire more people in key sectors, and hearing more AI complementing labor than substituting. Bowman's 10:50 AM ET remarks produced no market-moving headlines in coverage. Two-year Treasury yields are headed for their biggest weekly jump in two years.
headlines.why_it_matters: Collins offered no pushback on the three-hike repricing, so the market's next rate signal comes from Daly at noon ET and Jefferson at 7 PM ET — a hawkish tone would extend the selloff.

headlines.headline: Megacaps split as the tape faded: AAPL hit a new 52-week high of $360.83 and is +0.76% at $357.56; META +1.08% at $630.33 — while GOOGL fell -1.70% to $293.63, TSLA -2.24% to $388.54 after touching $404.40 at the open, and AMZN -1.25% at $264.09. GLJ Research reiterated a Sell on TSLA today.
headlines.why_it_matters: Apple and Meta are the only green megacaps left — the rotation that held the tape up at the open is narrowing as the selloff broadens.

headlines.headline: Cisco reported fiscal Q2 revenue of about $18.1 billion and raised its annual guidance, but shares fell 2% after lower Q1 gross margins.
headlines.why_it_matters: A guidance raise losing to a margin miss shows the tape is punishing any softness in profitability, even from a non-AI bellwether.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news this morning. Carried forward: record Q3 reported Nov 3 (revenue $357.2M, +43% YoY vs ~$348.1M consensus; Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M; DCF coverage 1.67x; EPS $0.33, ~$0.03 beat), $0.525 per-unit distribution paid Fri Nov 6, full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M, J-W Power acquisition closed (~$860M, ~4.4M combined horsepower). Fresh angle: a Simply Wall St analysis today frames USAC near fair value on a DCF basis at ~$24.92, with the debate now whether the record cash generation is already priced in. USAC slipped below its 50-day moving average on Nov 12 and its momentum indicator turned negative the same day. Next earnings Feb 16, 2027.
